title: token-level-observability-dashboard-and-alert-tuning
author: Evan Park
description:
Motivation: Our SLOs are defined at the token level for many streaming workloads, but we lack consistent token-level metrics and dashboards to diagnose latency and cost regressions. This PR provides a set of Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry trace hooks, Grafana dashboards, and tuned alert rules to give SREs and engineers actionable token-level visibility.

What this PR does: - Adds token-level latency histograms (redwood_token_latency_bucket, summary) with route/model labels and sampling controls. - Emits token_cost_per_route and token_count_by_model metrics to enable per-route cost breakdowns in dashboards and billing reports. - Adds OpenTelemetry span attributes on the token generation hot path to link tokens -> request traces (token_index, kv_cache_hit, batch_id). - Exposes a new /debug/observability-sampling endpoint to adjust trace sampling during incidents. - Introduces Grafana dashboard panels: Token latency heatmap, Token cost waterfall (per-route, per-model), Token-level latency percentiles by model and route, and a combined trace->token correlation view. - Tuned alerting rules: token_latency_sustained_regression (2m P95 increase > 25%), token_cost_spike (3x baseline sustained 5m), and kv_cache_miss_rate (>=5% for 10m). - Adds a rollout plan and feature flag (feature.token_observability) to enable the new metrics incrementally.

Checklist: - [x] Prometheus metric definitions and registry registration. - [x] OpenTelemetry span annotations and sampling controls. - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and variables. - [x] Alert rules and runbook links. - [x] Unit and integration tests for metric emission. - [x] Migration & rollout plan included.

Testing: Unit tests added for metric labels and histograms (observability/token_metrics_test.go). Integration smoke tests run in staging generate expected metrics under load. Manual QA: validated dashboard panels with staging traffic and created simulated alert conditions to validate runbooks and paging behavior.

Rollout plan: - Merge behind feature flag. - Stage enablement to canary region for 48h with increased sampling. - If no regressions, enable globally and turn sampling back to default. - Disable feature flag immediately if unexpected cost or cardinality spikes occur.

Backward compatibility: All changes are additive. Metrics are guarded by the feature flag and default to off for older clusters.

Related: ENG-1428 (observability token-level initiative), SUP-789 (customer case that drove alert tuning).

review_comments: Amelia Chen: Please confirm that we guard high-cardinality label values; route and model are safe as-is? I recommend adding cardinality bucketing for model_version. - Addressed in token_metrics.go, we map model_version -> major_minor and added a tests. (Evan)
Diego Martinez: Can we expose sampling toggle via admin console as well? - I added a small UI toggle in TokenDashboard.tsx and wired it to the /debug endpoint. (Evan)
Priya Singh: Alert thresholds look reasonable but please include a canary-only alert for initial rollout to avoid global paging. - Added token_latency_canary rule scoped to canary region. (Evan)
Liam O'Rourke: CI flaked on lint previously; fixed style nits and re-ran. Approving pending green CI. - (approved)
release_notes: Add token-level observability: new metrics (token latency histograms, token cost per route), Grafana dashboards for token-level debugging, and tuned alerts with runbooks. Metrics rollout behind feature flag. Improves SREs' ability to diagnose token-level regressions.
notes_for_ops:
Dashboard URL (staging): https://grafana.staging.redwood.example/d/token-level
Dashboard URL (prod will be available after rollout). Alert runbooks: docs/observability/runbooks/token_latency.md. Feature flag: feature.token_observability (default off). Sampling endpoint: POST /debug/observability-sampling {"rate":0.5}. If token metric cardinality spikes, disable flag and run the cardinality cleanup job in scripts/catalog/cardinality_cleanup.sh.
